annotations.text:
B + C blend
Structure from B: versus scoreboard header, dense leaderboard, HUD readout inside the viewer, event ticks on the scrub, portrait tiles with health bars.
Voice from C: bone-on-black with blood red, Anton titles and hero numbers, Oswald labels, campaign poster tiles, film sprockets around the viewer.
Roles: red is interactive and infected, gold is rating only, teal is survivor health only. Amber is retired.
Open questions for the spec: does the campaign tile row belong on every page or only Home and Campaigns; how much sepia the map art can take before infected dots lose contrast.

A · Safe room wall
Graffiti headers, typewritten sheets taped to concrete, polaroid rosters.
Why: the most instantly L4D thing there is, and it gives every page a reason to look handmade.
Tradeoff: loud. Rotated paper and marker type fight dense stat tables, so the leaderboard has to stay small or go plain.

B · Versus HUD
Keeps the original tokens (warm black, sodium amber, Barlow Condensed) and borrows the game's HUD grammar: a versus scoreboard header, portrait tiles with health bars, event ticks on the scrub bar, grain and vignette instead of flat panels.
Why: reads as competitive and lets the numbers stay the content. Smallest rebuild.
Tradeoff: the least theatrical of the three; the identity comes from details, not a big gesture.

C · Campaign poster
Movie-poster type (Anton), bone-on-black, blood-red rules, credits blocks, film sprockets around the viewer, each campaign as a poster tile.
Why: the strongest single gesture, and campaigns become the organizing idea of the site.
Tradeoff: the heavy vignette and sepia darken the map art, and Roman-numeral ranks stop working past a dozen rows.
